Move nodes in a tree

Source: R/trees.R
tree_move.Rd

Restructures a tree by updating parent_id fields and adding missing nodes based on move operations. Move operations are defined by a current path and a target path.

Usage

tree_move(data, moves, keep = TRUE, delim = ">")

Arguments

data

A data frame with the current tree. The columns id, parent_id, and lemma are necessary. For move operations crossing tree types, provide a type column. Other columns are allowed and preserved in the output.

moves

A data frame with the two columns from_path and to_path. Optionally, a to_type column can be provided to move nodes to a different tree type.

keep

Whether to keep the columns from_path and tree_path in the resulting data frame (TRUE) or to drop them (FALSE).

delim

The delimiter to use for the tree path (default is ">").

Value

A data frame with updated parent IDs, based on the move operations. Missing parent nodes are created.

Examples

data <- data.frame(
  id        = c("A", "B", "C"),
  parent_id = c(NA, "A", "B"),
  lemma     = c("A", "B", "C"),
  type      = "example"
)
moves <- data.frame(
  from_path = "A > B",
  to_path   = "X > Y > B"
)
tree_move(data, moves)
#> Ignoring moves with unknown from_path: 
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>   id                          norm_iri tree_path parent_id lemma type  from_path
#>   <chr>                       <chr>    <chr>     <chr>     <chr> <chr> <chr>    
#> 1 A                           NA       A         NA        A     exam… A        
#> 2 properties/example/tidy~x   tidy~x   X         NA        X     exam… X        
#> 3 properties/example/tidy~x-y tidy~x-y X > Y     properti… Y     exam… X > Y    
#> 4 B                           NA       X > Y > B properti… B     exam… A > B    
#> 5 C                           NA       X > Y > … B         C     exam… A > B > C
